title: Check yourself: Sessions, environment variables and the practice

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A developer adds a header that reads a new environment name in the shared connection settings and leaves the team write-up alone. What does the practice's grading do?

options.text: The credentials case fails, since each new variable needs a default value
options.says: Ruled out because the token has no default: "The token has none, because a default for a token would be a credential in the file".

options.text: The documentation case fails, because one of the variables the servers use is unlisted
options.says: The note has to list every variable: "every variable that appears in `.mcp.json` has to appear in the note."

options.text: Nothing fails, since the write-up is advice that the grading never reads
options.says: Ruled out because the note is checked: "The check turns a convention into a rule that fails when someone adds a variable and forgets the note."

options.text: The server case fails, since a header may not refer to any variable
options.says: Ruled out because a shared file does refer to variables: "A committed `.mcp.json` refers to variables and cannot hold their values."

origin.section: The environment is part of the setup

questions.stem: Which allow rule for the tracker passes the practice's read-only case?

options.says: Ruled out because a whole-server rule approves more than reading: "the ticket tools that change data are denied and only the reading ones are allowed"
Ruled out because a wildcard allows every tool: "every allowed ticket tool is a get, list or search tool".
Ruled out because creating is denied: "the create and delete tools are denied".
A get tool, with the create and delete tools denied.

origin.section: The practice: correct a draft setup

questions.stem: A new colleague clones the repository, and the ticket tools answer with an authorization error. The shared configuration is committed. What should the repository hold to prevent this?

options.text: A default for the token, written into the shared project file
options.says: Ruled out because a default for a token is a credential in the file: "a default for a token would be a credential in the file".

options.text: A team note that names every variable that the servers need to start
options.says: A note makes the missing variables visible.

options.text: A private copy of the project file with a working token in it, kept outside version control
options.says: Ruled out because a second copy defeats the shared file: "The file exists to be shared".

options.text: A line in the root memory file that holds a shared token
options.says: Ruled out because a committed file cannot hold a value: "A committed `.mcp.json` refers to variables and cannot hold their values."
